questions.prompt: Isotopes of an element have the same number of ___ but different numbers of ___.
questions.explain: Same protons (same element), different neutrons (different mass).

questions.prompt: How many neutrons are in carbon-14 (atomic number 6)?
Are these pairs isotopes of the same element?
questions.explain: Isotopes must be the same element (same protons). Argon-40 and calcium-40 are isobars (same mass number, different elements).

questions.prompt: Chlorine is 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is its average atomic mass?
Why do isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties?
options: They have the same number and arrangement of electrons
They have the same number of neutrons
questions.explain: Chemical properties depend on electrons, which are the same for all isotopes of an element.

questions.prompt: Match each isotope to its use.
questions.explain: Radioactive isotopes have many uses in medicine, energy and archaeology.

options: Isotopes have different numbers of electrons
questions.explain: Only some isotopes are radioactive; most are stable.

questions.prompt: Explain why the atomic mass of chlorine on the periodic table is 35.5 and not a whole number.
questions.modelAnswer: Chlorine exists as two isotopes, chlorine-35 and chlorine-37. Natural chlorine is a mixture (about 75% Cl-35 and 25% Cl-37), so the atomic mass is a weighted average of the two, which is 35.5.
rubric: Natural chlorine is a mixture of them in different amounts
The atomic mass is a weighted average
questions.explain: Relative atomic mass is an average over the natural isotopes.
